cases.note: the newest fitting rule answers, and a rule that did not answer keeps its place in its answers
a pattern fits only arguments of its own length; rules come before the otherwise answer
rules belong to one double and one method; an empty answer can be scripted
a sequence of answers, then its last answer for every later call
every call is recorded, whatever answered it; calls to a missing double are not
the nth call counts from the first or, when negative, from the last; zero and out of range are empty
an ordered check needs one distinct call per step, in order, with others allowed between
counts and calls grow as the code under test keeps calling
expectations answer in the order they were set, each up to its count; then the call is unexpected
the oldest expectation that fits and has calls left answers, even when a later one is more specific
only mocks take expectations; one name is one double, of either kind
a stubbed call is allowed and never reported; past its count an expected call falls back to the stub rules
verifyAll lists the mocks in the order they were made; checking twice changes nothing; the spy questions see every call
a repeating timer goes back in line when it fires, so a timer scheduled before that goes first at a tie
timers call the double like the code under test would: stubs answer, mocks check, spies record
a zero delay waits for the next advance, a timer due at the end of an advance fires, and the clock lands on the end
cancel stops a pending timer once; a fired one-shot and an unknown id cannot be cancelled
times beyond 32 bits, and one advance that fires a repeating timer many times
pending lists timers in the order they would fire, across delays and ties
